title: xfunc roadmap sparring notes — handoff prep
content:
Context / why I wrote this (notes to self):
- This is a preparatory sparring doc for the cross-team roadmap alignment meeting with Product, Eng (serving/runtime, infra), and Applied ML. Goal: reduce ambiguous asks and leave with a prioritized, executable 6-week plan + clear owners.
- Primary tension: shipping a hosted feature (low latency requirement) vs. Dedicated/Private customers who need predictable throughput and additional security work.
- Secondary tension: applied-ML wants to push a quantized Llama variant that reduces cost but hasn't been stress-tested on long-context workloads.

Meeting goals (what I want to see by EOD):
1) Agree on top 3 roadmap bets for the next 6 weeks, with measurable success criteria.
2) Decide whether Mode A (fast host-first) or Mode B (concurrency-first for Dedicated) is lead — or adopt explicit dual-track with canaries.
3) Capture immediate blockers and owners for infra + ML experiments (capacity estimates, perf runbook).
4) Identify any customer-impacting deprecations and schedule comms.

Proposed agenda (30–45m):
- 0–5m: Quick context + accept goals (me)
- 5–12m: Product priorities (Maya) — top customer asks, revenue/ARR signals, SLAs customers need
- 12–22m: Eng constraints (Ravi) — capacity, SLOs, current queues, rollout windows
- 22–30m: Applied ML experiments (Lina) — quantized model perf summary, known failure modes
- 30–38m: Crosswalk on tradeoffs & proposal (me) — lean plan A/B, gating metrics
- 38–45m: Decisions and next actions (assign owners)

Anchor metrics (pick 1–2 per bet):
- Latency p50/p95 for 1k token response on hosted: target <= 220ms p50, <= 600ms p95
- Cost per 1M generation tokens for hosted: target reduction of 18% vs baseline
- Dedicated throughput: sustain 350 concurrent sessions with <2% error rate
- Model quality: pass automated evals on 3 prompt suites (safety, hallucination, code) with <2% regression

Options I want us to consider (rough sketches):
- A: Host-first with quantized variant + autoscaling tweaks. Pros: fast to market, immediate cost wins. Cons: unknown long-context regressions, may need fallback to full-precision models.
- B: Dedicated-first (focus infra/throughput), longer runway but fewer regressions for enterprise customers. Pros: predictable SLOs for big customers. Cons: delayed cost savings for hosted.
- C: Dual-track hybrid: deploy quantized on hosted behind a canary flag + route Dedicated to stable full-precision until ML certs pass. Need explicit routing policy & rollback.

Risks I want to call out during the meeting (short bullets):
- Quantization regressions on code/composition prompts (applied-ml has a couple failing cases).
- Capacity modeling assumptions: Ravi's cost model assumes average sequence length 300; product is seeing longer tails on new features (800+).
- Rollout complexity: multi-model routing + per-customer pinning increases operational burden; SRE/console work needed to expose safe toggles.
- Comms risk: enterprise customers on Dedicated might be upset if hosted shows large improvements while Dedicated lags.

Concrete proposal (my lean ask):
- Proceed with Option C (dual-track) but with strict gating: only enable quantized hosted canary after passing a 72-hour perf+quality gate and a 1000-request stress run covering <1% regression on evals.
- Parallel work: SRE to add a temporary routing toggle (per-customer, feature-flag style) + runbook for fallback.
- Product to identify the top 2 enterprise accounts that need Dedicated parity and map their must-have SLOs.

Pre-meeting facts to surface (I will call these out quickly):
- Baseline hosted CPU/GPU cost numbers (last 7d) and avg response length (source: infra-costs dashboard).
- Recent applied-ml eval snapshot (ML-237): quantized variant fails on 2/30 code prompts — details in linked JIRA.
- Outstanding infra tickets that block routing changes: ENG-4821 (console toggle), ENG-4892 (canary autoscaler).

Decision points (explicit asks during meeting):
- Do we greenlight the canary window for hosted quantized? (Yes / No / Need to define extra gating)
- If No, do we instead prioritize Dedicated throughput work?
- Who will own the 6-week plan and deliver the weekly checkpoints?

Draft 6-week milestones (high level):
Week 1: finalize experiment plan, wire up console toggle, agree on gating metrics, run a short perf test on a 1000-req sample
Week 2–3: host canary enable, run 72-hour perf+eval gate, collect telemetry, triage regressions
Week 4: Dedicated infra improvements begin (autoscaler tuning, throughput tests), customer comms drafted for potential differences
Week 5: Decide GA for hosted quantized or roll back; finalize Dedicated rollout timeline
Week 6: GA release for hosted or definitive roll-back + retro & postmortem checklist

Follow-ups / Action items (quick table — owner, action, due):
- Ravi: provide updated capacity model with 95th percentile sequence-length assumptions by 2026-09-29
- Lina: produce a 500-sample failure catalogue for quantized model (annotated) by 2026-09-28
- Maya: confirm top-2 enterprise parity requirements and contacts by 2026-09-27
- Emma (me): draft canary runbook + rollback checklist and share w/ SRE by 2026-09-26
- Kai: create dashboard tile for quantized vs baseline latency + error rates by 2026-09-30

Notes — things I should remember to say / stick to during sparring:
- Emphasize we are accepting small, measurable risk for a scoped canary — not full global switch.
- Ask Applied-ML to surface test cases that represent long-context composition (ask for minimal reproducer).
- Ask Eng to quantify ops cost for dual-model routing in dev and prod.

Open questions (need answers before final plan):
- How many Dedicated customers currently require model parity to avoid regressions? (Product)
- Is there a supported path to automatically fallback per-request if a quantized output fails QA checks? (Eng/SRE)
- Can we run perf experiments on a matched traffic replay for 48–72h to get realistic tails? (Infra)

References + quick links (call out in meeting):
- CONFLUENCE:INF-ROADMAP-2026 (planning notes)
- JIRA ENG-4821 (console toggle) / ML-237 (quantization eval)
- Slack thread: #platform-roadmap / thread ts-169 (customer asks)

My post-meeting plan (how I'll follow up):
- Send concise recap with decisions + owners within 24 hours.
- Add agreed milestones to the xfunc roadmap board and tag owners.
- Set a 15-min weekly checkpoint (Wednesdays) for quick unblock checks.

Scratchpad detritus (things I might clean up later):
- Try combining p95 latency gating with per-model quality score to avoid misaligned goals.
- Explore small-budget pilot to run quantized model on a private deployment (low-risk customer) to simulate enterprise constraints.
- Note: possible doc to prepare for customers that explains tradeoffs in plain language (avoid technical jargon).

End — leave this doc open during the sparring session and annotate decisions inline.
